title: Turning Agent Memory Into Skills That Work — Will Lyon, Neo4j
talk_summary: Will Lyon argues agent memory should be a connected, typed, traceable context graph with short-term, long-term, and reasoning memory, not just embedding retrieval. He shows distilling scoped decision traces into governed, executable skills, including a typed execution-graph representation and staleness curation.

takeaways.technique: Decision traces as first-class reasoning memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Persist each agent decision linked to evidence, policies, tool calls, results, token use, and timing so runs can be debugged and reused across agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every decision uh that our agent makes is linked to uh the reasoning grounded in evidence

takeaways.what_they_do: Scope a memory subgraph around an entity, conversation, or project, then distill it into a skill grounded in actual observed tool calls and entities rather than freeform prose.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to distill that into a skill, but not just like a markdown file

takeaways.what_they_do: Represent skills as graphs of executable steps with strict schemas and metadata, extending the agent-skills format with typed nodes and governed descriptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: treats your skills as typed execution graphs. Right? So we have uh steps modeled as nodes

takeaways.what_they_do: Link skill components to underlying memory and run background curation to surface stale, drifted, or contradictory skills; retrieve the latest governed skill dynamically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: surface when uh our skills become stale based on the data that we have in the memory system

takeaways.what_they_do: Persist agent runs and decision traces in one shared graph so many agents with shared tools can learn from each other's prior decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one shared context graph uh that enables our agents to essentially learn from uh each other

takeaways.what_they_do: Use deterministic steps for extraction, validation, and graph construction, reserving the LLM mainly for synthesizing claims and skill descriptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of these steps are deterministic. Um we're really only leveraging an LLM here uh for synthesizing some of the claims
